feed.title: UW Planetary Mineral Physics Laboratory
feed.subtitle: The UW Planetary Mineral Physics Laboratory studies water, ices and minerals at the extreme conditions of planets and moons to understand the evolution and habitability of icy and ocean worlds, support their exploration, and inform fields from environmental science to biomedical engineering.

entry.title: Titan’s tidal dissipation precludes a subsurface ocean, in Nature

link.title: Titan’s tidal dissipation precludes a subsurface ocean, in Nature

entry.content:
Our paper with F. Petricca and colleagues, published in Nature, shows that the strong tidal dissipation revealed by Cassini data precludes a subsurface ocean on Titan.

The study was covered by PBS / Associated Press, Smithsonian Magazine, Gizmodo, GeekWire, UW News, Le Figaro and Sciences et Avenir.
entry.summary: Our paper with F. Petricca and colleagues, published in Nature, shows that the strong tidal dissipation revealed by Cassini data precludes a subsurface ocean on Titan.

entry.title: New salty ices make headlines
entry.content: Our discovery of hyperhydrated sodium chloride hydrates, stable at icy moon surface conditions and published in PNAS, was covered by CNN and the New York Times.
